package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious Windows executables, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: Both Bisamware and Chile Locker are ransomware families that encrypt user files, demand ransom for decryption, and employ anti-recovery techniques such as deleting shadow copies. They are distributed via malicious documents exploiting vulnerabilities (Bisamware) or through other unknown vectors (Chile Locker). Their sole purpose is extortion and data destruction, with no legitimate functionality.

execution_context.trigger: At document open-time (user opens malicious Word document)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious Microsoft Word file exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina vulnerability)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ms-msdt:/id PCWDiagnostic?form=... (malicious MSDT URI embedded in Word document to trigger code execution via Follina exploit)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open-time, the code abuses the ms-msdt URI scheme to invoke the Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool, downloads a remote payload from an attacker-controlled server, and executes it on the victim's system, resulting in initial ransomware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate documents should not invoke system diagnostic tools or trigger remote code execution via URI handlers. The use of ms-msdt from a document is a known exploitation vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents do not execute system-level commands or download and run code without explicit user action.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: MSDT may be legitimately invoked by administrators for troubleshooting, but never via unsolicited documents or in a way that downloads and executes arbitrary code.
key_indicators: Abuse of ms-msdt URI scheme in Office document
Remote code execution triggered by document open
No user consent for code execution

execution_context.trigger: At payload execution-time (after remote code execution)
execution_context.file_location: Ransomware executable (Bisamware/Chile Locker main binary, typically dropped in %TEMP% or user profile directories)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Enumerate user files, encrypt contents using symmetric encryption (e.g., AES), and append .BISAMWARE or .crypt extension to each file.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At payload execution-time, the ransomware enumerates user files across local and mapped drives, encrypts their contents using a symmetric encryption algorithm, and appends a unique extension (.BISAMWARE or .crypt) to each file, rendering them inaccessible without the decryption key.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Mass file encryption with a ransom extension is a definitive indicator of ransomware activity. The process occurs without user consent and targets a wide range of file types.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not encrypt user files in bulk or alter file extensions without explicit user intent and clear notification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encryption utilities may encrypt files, but only with explicit user action, clear user interface, and without ransom demands or extension changes.
key_indicators: Addition of unique ransomware extension (.BISAMWARE or .crypt)
Encryption of common document, image, and archive file types

execution_context.file_location: Filesystem root or affected user directories (e.g., Desktop, Documents)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Create ransom note files named SYSTEM=RANSOMWARE=INFECTED.txt or readme_for_unlock.txt with payment instructions.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Immediately after file encryption, the ransomware creates ransom note files (e.g., SYSTEM=RANSOMWARE=INFECTED.txt or readme_for_unlock.txt) in affected directories, instructing the victim to contact the attacker via a TOR chat room or site to purchase a decryption key.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Creation of ransom notes demanding payment and providing instructions for contacting the attacker is a direct and unambiguous indicator of ransomware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not extort users or create threatening ransom notes with payment instructions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; ransom notes with extortion demands are unique to ransomware and extortionware.
key_indicators: Presence of ransom note files with specific names
Instructions to contact attacker via TOR or anonymous channels
Explicit payment demand for file decryption

execution_context.trigger: After file encryption and ransom note creation (pre-exit)
execution_context.file_location: System (Windows Volume Shadow Copies, accessed via vssadmin.exe)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After file encryption and ransom note creation, the ransomware executes the system command 'vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet' to delete all Windows shadow copies, thereby preventing recovery of files via built-in backup mechanisms.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting all shadow copies is a well-known anti-recovery tactic used by ransomware to increase the likelihood of ransom payment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not indiscriminately delete system backups or shadow copies, especially without user consent or notification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may clear shadow copies for maintenance, but not in conjunction with mass file encryption or without user awareness.
key_indicators: Execution of vssadmin.exe with delete shadows parameters
No user consent or notification for backup deletion
Command executed immediately after file encryption and ransom note creation

attack_chain.action: User opens a malicious Microsoft Word document exploiting CVE-2022-30190 (Follina), which triggers the ms-msdt URI handler.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and download of the ransomware payload.

attack_chain.action: Ransomware payload is downloaded and executed on the victim's machine via the exploited MSDT handler.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initiation of the file encryption process.

attack_chain.action: Ransomware enumerates and encrypts user files, appending a unique extension (.BISAMWARE or .crypt) to each file.
attack_chain.leads_to: User files become inaccessible without the decryption key.

attack_chain.action: Ransomware creates ransom note files in affected directories, instructing the victim to contact the attacker for decryption.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is extorted for payment and provided with instructions to contact the attacker.

attack_chain.action: Ransomware deletes all Windows shadow copies to prevent file recovery via system backups.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim cannot restore files from backups, increasing extortion pressure.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of ms-msdt URI handler from Office documents (indicative of Follina/CVE-2022-30190 exploitation)
Bulk file encryption with new extensions (.BISAMWARE, .crypt) across user directories
Creation of ransom note files (SYSTEM=RANSOMWARE=INFECTED.txt, readme_for_unlock.txt) in user-accessible locations
Execution of vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet immediately after file encryption
network_indicators: Outbound connections to TOR network for ransom payment instructions
Potential C2 or payload download URLs embedded in malicious documents (as observed in Follina exploitation chains)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents invoking ms-msdt or other unusual URI handlers, especially those matching Follina exploit patterns. Detect mass file renaming and encryption with .BISAMWARE or .crypt extensions across user directories. Alert on creation of known ransom note filenames (SYSTEM=RANSOMWARE=INFECTED.txt, readme_for_unlock.txt) in user-accessible locations. Monitor for execution of vssadmin.exe with parameters to delete shadow copies, particularly when occurring immediately after file encryption. Network monitoring should flag connections to TOR or suspicious external endpoints following document execution, and inspect Office documents for embedded exploit URLs.
